evidence: starci-academy-fe/src has no cart and no installment surface of any kind. All of it is net-new on this frontend.

The backend installment domain ships end to end: installment_plans entity, two enums, InstallmentPlanService, a daily enforcement cron, checkout integration on all three purchase entry points, myInstallmentPlans, payNextInstallment, webhook and reconcile settlement, and reminder/default emails.

Exactly ONE term is offered: 3 months at 10% markup (installment.markupPercentByMonths has a single key). The config comment records a teacher decision of 2026-07-14 dropping 6- and 12-month terms so no term picker is needed.
computeInstallmentTotal derives totalAmountVnd = base x 1.10 and monthlyAmountVnd = total / months - an EQUAL split of 36.67% of base per cycle.
computeMinPaymentVnd for a Fixed plan returns the single stored monthlyAmountVnd, and installment_plans has no per-cycle amount column, so a 50/30/30 schedule is not representable today.

The markup is dropped from 10% to 5% by teacher decision. Shares must sum to 100 + markup, so 105 rather than 110: 50 + 30 + 30 no longer closes and would overcharge by five points of base. Keeping the instructed 50% first cycle, the remaining 55 splits evenly into 27.5 / 27.5.

At 5% with 50 / 27.5 / 27.5 the learner's mean outstanding balance is 41.25% of base and the effective rate is about 12.1% per two months (~72% nominal annual) - roughly half the ~133% of the 10% front-loaded plan and below the ~109% of what ships today.

The financing cost of carrying a mean 2.042.000d for two months at Vietnamese short-term rates is on the order of 30.000d against a 247.500d fee, so 5% covers financing many times over and the surplus pays for default risk and the enforcement machinery.
Nothing is charged automatically. There is no card on file anywhere in the codebase; cycles 2 and 3 are manual payNextInstallment checkouts the learner starts.
There is no calendar: the plan holds one rolling nextDueAt advanced +1 month from the payment that just landed, so cycle 3's date does not exist until cycle 2 is paid.
lockedCourseIds is every course of the order, so missing a cycle locks all courses bought together.

A locked-for-non-payment enrollment and a never-paid trial are the same is_enrolled = false with nothing recording why; a locked state can only be rendered by cross-referencing myInstallmentPlans for a Defaulted plan.
coursesCheckoutPreview already returns installmentOptions for the whole order - the earlier reading of that file in this plan run missed the field.
TransactionStatus.Cancelled and .Failed are declared but never assigned; every real failure lands on Unpaid.
Cart checkout accepts no voucherCode; only the single-course courseEnroll does.
Outside production every VND amount is divided by 100 before reaching the frontend, so amounts arrive display-ready and must never be re-scaled locally.
starci-academy CartPage and MiniCartDrawer show only a hint built from the cheapest monthlyAmountVnd and defer the real choice to PaymentModal.

Legacy PaymentModal initialises installmentMonths to null - the comment reads 'pay in full (unchanged default)' - and resets it to null on every modal open, so defaulting to installments is a real departure from the reference.

hasUsd is false whenever an installment term is active, because installments are VND-only per PAYMENT_MODIFIER_CAPABILITY. Defaulting to installments therefore HIDES Stripe, PayPal and Crypto from the gateway list until the buyer switches back to paying in full.
starci-academy-fe has ModalShell but no DrawerShell, so the drawer needs the one shell canon names and this repository has not built.
unknowns: SETTLED: the markup is 5% and the first cycle is 50%, giving a 50 / 27.5 / 27.5 vector. The remaining judgement, if anyone wants to revisit it, is 45/30/30 - same 105 total, a lower entry price, and less collected before the riskiest moment. Full arithmetic in installment-analysis.md.

How many buyers actually choose installments. The fee halves and direction D makes installments opt-in rather than default, so revenue from the plan drops on both counts; nobody in this run has the take-up number that would size it.

Whether hiding the international gateways by default is acceptable. Installments are VND-only, so opening on them removes Stripe, PayPal and Crypto from the list until the buyer switches back - which is a real cost for any buyer who would have paid in USD.

RESOLVED BY THE SELECTION: pre-selecting the option that costs 5% more would earn 247.500d per worked cart from every buyer who does not notice, and pre-ticked paid options are restricted in several consumer-protection regimes. Directions A, B and C took that position; the selected direction D does not.

Whether a plans surface (list, pay next cycle, locked-course recovery) is in scope with the cart or is its own later plan. Offering installments in the cart creates an obligation this frontend currently has nowhere to discharge.
What a signed-out reader gets on add-to-cart. Legacy defers the intent and replays it after sign-in, which is generous and is also a second state machine.
Whether a learner may open a second installment plan while one is still Active. Nothing in the read code forbids it and nobody has decided it.
Where coursesCheckout sends the reader after the gateway. The legacy drawer hands to a payment overlay this repository does not have.

directions.thesis: Keep legacy's division of labour - the cart states a price, the payment step states how to pay - but open on installments so nobody has to find them.
directions.primaryCta: Thanh toan in the cart, then Tra ky 1 - 2.475.000d in the payment modal
tradeoffs: The smallest edit to legacy that still makes installments the default.
The cart stays short: one summary block, no schedule, no switch.
The buyer sees the three cycles only after leaving the cart, which is the latest possible moment to meet them.
The default silently drops Stripe, PayPal and Crypto from the gateway list.
legacyDivergence: Opens on installments where legacy opens on paying in full and resets to it on every modal open.
The cart total becomes the installment total, so the number does not jump between the cart and the modal.
The 'chi tu X/thang' hint cannot survive: under 50/30/30 the first cycle is the most expensive one, so a from-price would be a false floor.
The schedule shows relative offsets rather than hard dates, because the server holds one rolling nextDueAt and not a calendar.
The lockout warning names all courses in the order, because one plan gates the whole checkout.

contracts.why: A section label and its quiet end action stay outside the surface they name.
Cited as the joined-list precedent: comparable rows in one surface, shared separators, one row grammar.
A figure and the words that qualify it are one statement, so they stack.
One purchasable row is a fixed grammar - thumbnail, name over tier, charged over list, remove - and it must read the same at both measures.
Subtotal, surcharge and total are one statement whose last line is set apart, so the separator belongs to the contract rather than to a caller.
A cycle is an ordinal, a timing, a share and an amount; the row that is due now is marked by state rather than by a different shape, so the same row renders a forecast and a live plan.

vocabularyProposals.name: InstallmentSchedule
vocabularyProposals.meaning: The cycles of a plan - as a forecast before purchase, and as a live record afterwards.
vocabularyProposals.absenceDefault: An empty cycles array renders nothing, which is what a free or USD-only order must produce.
vocabularyProposals.precedence: Only cycle 1 carries a real date; later cycles carry offsets, because the server holds one rolling nextDueAt.
vocabularyProposals.why: A front-loaded schedule cannot be summarised by one per-month number, so the cycles have to be shown as rows - and the same rows later carry paid/due/overdue for a live plan.

vocabularyProposals.name: AddToCartButton
vocabularyProposals.meaning: The affordance on a course that starts the purchase flow.

vocabularyProposals.precedence: The signed-out decision lands here and nowhere else.
vocabularyProposals.why: Every direction starts here, and it is the only owner that has to know what a signed-out press means.

backendEnablerProposals.uiNeed: Lower the 3-month markup from 10% to 5%, and charge 50% of the base price at checkout with half the remainder on each of the two following cycles, instead of three equal cycles.
backendEnablerProposals.evidence: computeInstallmentTotal returns one monthlyAmountVnd = total/months (installment-plan.service.ts:100-112); computeMinPaymentVnd(Fixed) returns that single stored value (124-134); installment_plans has no per-cycle column (entity 192-253). The requested shape is not representable today. The markup itself is already env-driven (INSTALLMENT_MARKUP_PERCENT_3M) and needs only a value change.
backendEnablerProposals.proposal: Set INSTALLMENT_MARKUP_PERCENT_3M to 5. Configure the schedule as a BASIS-POINT share vector, INSTALLMENT_SCHEDULE_BPS_3M = 5000,2750,2750 - basis points rather than percents because 27.5 is not an integer and the surrounding columns are int. Have computeInstallmentTotal return cycles[] beside totalAmountVnd, snapshot the vector on the plan in a jsonb cycle_bps column beside the existing markup_percent snapshot, and make computeMinPaymentVnd(Fixed) read cycles[installmentsPaid] instead of a single monthly amount.
backendEnablerProposals.arithmetic: Shares are of the BASE (loyalty and bundle discounted) price and must sum to 100 + markup. At 5% that is 105, so the original 50/30/30 overshoots by five points of base. Keeping the instructed 50% first cycle leaves 55 to split evenly: 50 / 27.5 / 27.5. On the worked cart, 2.475.000 + 1.361.250 + 1.361.250 = 5.197.500 = 4.950.000 x 1.05, with no rounding remainder. The first cycle is unchanged from the 10% plan because it is 50% of base either way; the whole 247.500d saving lands on cycles 2 and 3.
backendEnablerProposals.authorization: Unchanged: the same buyer, the same domestic VND gateways.
backendEnablerProposals.compatibility: Live plans keep working, and this matters more now than before: markup_percent is already snapshotted per plan, so a buyer who bought at 10% keeps owing 10% and a plan with no vector keeps its even split. The 5% applies to new plans only; nobody is repriced in either direction.
